R: The horde's quota board: 40 AXES BY MOONFALL. Underneath, in Harrow's hand: "Sweetheart: never swung. Keep it that way."
r: Axes, forty of them, for the horde. Harrow hasn't sharpened a single one.
V: The forge's great bellows, torn and wheezing.
x: Coal, and a cracked mould for a crown: the Hale coronation crown, never finished.
A: A suit of armour, far too big for anyone. The size of a giant.
t: An anvil, worn to a curve by centuries of hammering.
1: The door back to the street.

objects.name: Old Harrow
lines: Forty axes by moonfall. For the horde. I haven't made one worth the name.
My bellows are shot, anyway. Can't do honest work, can't do dishonest work.

answer: Best sword my family ever made. Great-grandad's great-grandad forged it, for a big lad with the biggest hands anyone ever saw and the smallest courage.
It's the only sword we ever made that stayed clean. We're prouder of that than all the rest.
The king closed the Trial so nobody could challenge him. Oldest trick there is. Change the rules once you've won.
A body's the first tool you're given, and the only one you can't replace. Look after it, and when the day comes you have to stand your ground, it'll stand with you.

questions.ask: Even your bellows gave up on you.
answer: Aye. Wheezed their last on a Tuesday. I know how they felt.
Mind the anvil on your way out. It's still hot, even if I'm not.

lines: Bellows sing like new. Whoever fixed them knows their trade.
Bring me that big lad's armour. My family owes him a fitting. Five hundred years late, but it'll fit.
